title: Bupa Arabia invests US$22.4M in Saudi Arabia's orphan health insurance programme | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication

contentHtml:
SAUDI ARABIA— Bupa Arabia Cooperative Insurance Company has invested SAR 84 million (US$22.4 million) in health insurance for orphans since 2011, expanding access to medical care for thousands of children annually through its corporate social responsibility programme.

The company presented the programme’s progress at the Global CSR Forum 2026 in Riyadh, hosted by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development.

The initiative, which began by covering 18 children, now serves between 2,000 and 3,000 orphans annually, with more than 34,000 insurance policies issued to date.

Expanding healthcare access

Delivered in partnership with the ministry, the programme operates through 25 orphan care centres across 12 Saudi cities.

Coverage follows the standard health insurance policy approved by the Insurance Authority, with an annual limit of SAR 500,000 (US$133,300) per beneficiary.

Beneficiaries also receive support through a dedicated contact centre that facilitates pre-authorisations and claims.

The programme reviews exceptional requests for treatments that fall outside standard coverage limits, helping address individual medical needs.

In 2025, Bupa Arabia settled 22,985 medical claims worth SAR 11.5 million (US$3.07 million) and processed 11,911 pre-authorisation requests.

Medical evidence supported approval of 78.6% of these requests, while the company responded to 91% of requests within ten minutes.

Exceptional approvals have enabled access to treatments such as prosthetic limbs, finger implants, dental procedures and reconstructive surgery.

Bupa Arabia Chairman Eng. Loay Hisham Nazer said the company views corporate social responsibility as a sustained commitment to measurable outcomes rather than a series of isolated initiatives.

He highlighted continuity of care and the application of the insurer’s expertise to meet beneficiaries’ needs.

Broader community programmes

Beyond insurance, Bupa Arabia supports orphans through educational, employment-readiness and social initiatives.

Since 2023, it has provided school supplies to more than 200 orphans annually.

Career workshops have covered CV writing, interview preparation and job-search skills, benefiting 416 orphans in 2021 and more than 200 in 2025.

In 2025, 148 employee volunteers visited 300 orphans during Eid celebrations, distributing gifts and organising social activities.

The company also established a charitable endowment through the Ehsan platform, matching employee donations to increase contributions.

Other initiatives reached 314 people during activities marking the International Day of Persons with Disabilities.

Meanwhile, 94 volunteers visited patients with cancer and chronic diseases in hospitals in Jeddah, Riyadh and Al Khobar, while 75 volunteers engaged 230 older people living in care homes.

Bupa Arabia also supported vulnerable households by rebuilding nine homes, providing appliances to 49 brides, contributing to the Furejat debt-relief initiative through Ehsan and organising clothing donations with Kiswat Al-Sayida Aisha.

In 2025, 414 employees participated in donation initiatives, while between 320 and 400 employees take part in annual blood donation campaigns.

The company also launched an initiative in 2025 to sponsor orphans on behalf of employees and their families.

Its approach combines employee participation, partnerships with government agencies and healthcare providers, and performance monitoring to assess claims, response times, beneficiary reach and volunteer contributions.

In 2024, Bupa Arabia received the Silver Award for Corporate Social Responsibility.
